subtitle: BTC dominance (BTC.D) is the % of total crypto market cap that BTC represents. When BTC.D falls, capital is rotating into alts — 'alt season'. When BTC.D rises, capital flees alts back to BTC ('safety in BTC'). Read this rotation correctly and you'll know when to size up which type of position.

blocks.content:
The crypto market isn't monolithic. Within crypto, capital constantly rotates between BTC and alts. Sometimes alts outperform; sometimes they dramatically underperform. BTC dominance (BTC.D) measures this rotation directly.

For a trader, knowing whether you're in 'BTC season' or 'alt season' determines:

  • Which assets to focus on (BTC only? majors? mid-caps? small-caps?)
  • How aggressively to size alt positions
  • When to rotate profits from alts back to BTC (or vice versa)

BTC.D = BTC's market cap / Total crypto market cap × 100. It's expressed as a percentage. Historical range roughly 35-70%:

  • BTC.D 35-45% = peak alt season (alts massively outperforming)
  • BTC.D 45-55% = mid-range, mixed conditions
  • BTC.D 55-65% = BTC-dominated; alts struggling
  • BTC.D 65%+ = extreme BTC dominance (often during bear markets or major rotation events)

The TREND in BTC.D matters more than the absolute level. Rising BTC.D = capital fleeing alts. Falling BTC.D = capital flowing into alts.

blocks.title: Alt season = sustained outperformance of alts vs BTC
blocks.content:
It's not just 'alts going up'. Alt season specifically means:

  • Alts gaining FASTER than BTC for sustained period (weeks to months).
  • BTC.D falling consistently.
  • Mid-cap and small-cap alts often gaining 100-500% in weeks.
  • Retail attention shifts from BTC to alts (Twitter sentiment, search trends).

Alt seasons historically come AFTER BTC's main bull run completes. BTC makes its blow-off top; capital rotates down the cap ladder into ETH first, then majors, then mid-caps, then small-caps. The rotation can produce explosive moves in alts while BTC consolidates or even slowly declines.

blocks.content: How to read BTC.D for trading decisions

• BTC.D rising sharply (e.g., 3%+ in a week): capital is fleeing alts. REDUCE alt exposure. Either rotate to BTC or take profits.
  • BTC.D falling sharply: alt season in progress. Size up alts (within risk rules) — they may have multi-week outperformance.
  • BTC.D stable: no rotation signal. Trade individual setups on their merits.
  • BTC.D at extreme highs (65%+): alts have likely been crushed for months; either still in late bear or early reversal. Watch for stabilization before alt longs.
  • BTC.D at extreme lows (35-40%): alt season at maximum euphoria. Often a TOP SIGNAL — start taking alt profits.

blocks.title: Don't chase late alt season
blocks.content:
The last 5-10% of an alt-season rally produces the most dramatic-looking returns but is also the most dangerous. Retail piles in at peak euphoria; BTC.D bottoms; capital rotates back to BTC (or stables); alts crash 40-70% as the rotation reverses.

Signs you're in late alt season: dog/meme coins doing 10× weekly, random small-caps pumping on no news, social media universally bullish on alts, 'BTC.D will go to 30%' becomes consensus. When you see these, START taking profits — don't add more.

The highest-quality alt trades occur when:

  1. BTC.D is in a falling trend (alt rotation in progress).
  2. Macro is risk-on (broader global conditions supportive).
  3. BTC is in markup phase (not yet topping) OR consolidating after a top.
  4. The specific alt has its own technical setup (S/R, structure, indicators).
  5. Volume on the alt is rising (real participation, not just thin pumps).

When 4-5 of these align, the alt can run hard. When only 1-2 align (e.g., 'just BTC.D falling but macro risk-off'), expect smaller, choppier moves.
When to rotate profits BACK to BTC

If you've ridden alts during alt season, knowing when to rotate back to BTC (or stables) is critical. Signs to rotate out:

  • BTC.D starts rising consistently for 1-2 weeks (rotation reversal).
  • Your alt positions have made 100%+ — secure profits even if more upside seems possible.
  • Macro turning risk-off (DXY rising, VIX spiking).
  • BTC is showing distribution signs (Wyckoff lesson 33).
  • Social/sentiment universally bullish on alts (contrarian signal).

Rotating back to BTC during peak alt season is HARD psychologically — alts are still pumping and FOMO is intense. But it's exactly the time when the math (BTC.D bottoming + alt profits at max) tells you to.

Scenario: BTC just topped at $75K after a 6-month bull run. Currently $72K and consolidating. BTC.D has fallen from 56% to 51% over the last 3 weeks. ETH has rallied from $3,200 to $4,100 (28% gain) while BTC has been flat.

Interpretation: alt rotation has started. ETH is leading. Major alts will likely follow next. Mid-caps after that.

Strategy:

  • Continue holding BTC at reduced size (took profits at top).
  • Increase ETH allocation given the clear leadership.
  • Identify major alts with strong fundamentals (top 20-50 by cap) for the next rotation phase.
  • Monitor BTC.D weekly. If it continues falling, alt-season progression continues. If it suddenly reverses up, take alt profits and rotate back to BTC or stables.

blocks.title: Take this with you
blocks.content:
Three rules:

  1. Track BTC.D trend. Falling = alt rotation; rising = capital fleeing alts back to BTC.
  2. Trade WITH the rotation. Don't long alts when BTC.D is rising sharply; don't long BTC during peak alt season.
  3. Take alt profits during late alt season. When BTC.D is bottoming and meme coins are euphoric, the rotation back to BTC is near.
